newsitem.title: USA: Dow dodges data bullet to post slight midday rise.
newsitem.headline: Dow dodges data bullet to post slight midday rise.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were little changed at a quiet midsession Friday as markets shrugged off a surprisingly strong September durable goods report.
The Dow industrials rose 16 points to touch a session high of 6008 at midday. The Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 indices each eked out fractional gains.
The modest gains registered by stocks mirrored a somewhat surprisingly firm tone in the bond market, which rallied despite much stronger than expected monthly durable goods orders data.

The Commerce Department reported durable goods orders rose by a seasonally adjusted 4.6 percent in September -- more than double the 2.0 percent rate forecast by economists -- a figure that sent the inflation-wary bond market skidding.
However, cooler heads soon prevailed and bonds staged a quick recovery, eventually heading higher on the session.

"It was a very big number but you have to remember two things," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany, "it's a September number and it's a very, very volatile and unpredictable number."
Evidence of the report's volatility came in the Commerce Department's downward revision of the August figure to show a 3.5 percent decline in orders.
When the threat of the report had clearly safely passed, stocks spent most of the morning locked in tight ranges as markets braced for a heavy slate of economic data due next week.
However, analysts did warn the recent profit-taking pressure that has pulled the Dow industrials down some 100 points over in the past week is likely not over yet.
The company reported third quarter earnings of $0.95 per share, slightly above estimates, and expressed confidence about its fourth quarter sales and profit outlook.

Chubb Corp surged 5-7/8 to 51-3/8 after the company disclosed to analysts it was considering selling its life insurance and real estate businesses. Chubb declined to comment on the development. Alex Brown upgraded the shares to buy from attractive early today.
Etec Systems Inc plunged 10-7/8 to 25-1/8 after the company warned its first quarter earnings will be significantly lower than analysts' estimates.

Octel Communications Corp tumbled 8-5/8 to 15-7/8 after it reported weaker than expected first quarter earnings late Thursday. The voice processing systems company also told analysts that the release of an upcoming product upgrade would be delayed.
Early today, Merrill Lynch lowered its near-term rating on Octel to neutral from accumulate and its long-term rating to accumulate from buy.
